description: The pie chart presents the distribution of sources/outlets referenced in the paper “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” showing 16 slices in total, each labeled with a count displayed inside the slice. The largest slice is an unlabeled blue segment marked “14” (about 14% if treated as out of 100), followed by a gray “Other” slice marked “13” (about 13%). Two medium slices are “Drudge Report” in orange marked “8” (about 8%) and “The Daily Caller” in green marked “8” (about 8%), and another is “The Huffington Post” in red marked “7” (about 7%). Two slices labeled “NPR” (purple) and “Vox” (brown) are each marked “6” (about 6%), and two slices labeled “The Guardian” (pink) and “BBC” (light gray) are each marked “5” (about 5%). “RT” (yellow-green) is marked “4” (about 4%). A set of smaller slices near the bottom are each marked “3” (about 3%) and labeled “Daily Kos” (cyan), “National Review” (light blue), “Daily Mail” (orange), “Redstate” (green), “Fox News” (red), “CNN” (purple), “PoliticusUSA” (brown), and “Shareblue” (pink). The chart uses direct labels around the pie with numeric values inside slices, includes no separate legend, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized; the slices appear arranged roughly from larger segments on the right/top toward smaller segments clustered along the bottom.
